observations.pixelFacts: One graph, no separate panels. A solid vertical F axis rises with an arrow; one solid horizontal r axis points right and crosses at the origin. The source labels the origin 0, force F, distance r, and the net-force crossing r0. No numerical scales, units, measured coordinates, grid rows or columns are present.
observations.requiredRelationship: All three signed-force curves share the same F=0 horizontal line, distance direction and equilibrium position.

observations.pixelFacts: The rightmost steep upper solid curve stays above the horizontal axis and flattens toward it on the right. A solid leader points from the upper-right Chinese repulsion label to this curve.
observations.requiredRelationship: Positive repulsive component, large at short distances, decreasing toward zero at larger distance.

observations.pixelFacts: A solid lower curve starts near the bottom, rises rightward and remains below the horizontal axis. A solid leader joins its rising portion to the lower-right Chinese attraction label.
observations.requiredRelationship: Negative attractive component whose magnitude decreases at larger distance.

observations.pixelFacts: A middle solid curve starts above the axis to the left of the repulsive component, crosses the axis beside r0, reaches a rounded negative minimum, then rises between the axis and the attractive component. The upper-left Chinese interaction-force label has a solid leader to its upper branch.
observations.requiredRelationship: Net equals the signed sum of the two components; positive to the left of r0, zero at r0, negative to the right, with a negative trough and a tail tending to zero.

observations.pixelFacts: A short section of the net curve through and around the r0 crossing is visibly thicker than the rest. It follows the same descending curve, rather than forming a second force curve or a whole-range straight line.
observations.requiredRelationship: Preserve a local net-force emphasis supporting the nearby-linear approximation only near equilibrium.

observations.pixelFacts: Unlabelled dashed strokes are distinct from the solid axes, force curves and label leaders. A positive and negative dashed level begin on the F axis, bend to meet the r axis at a left reference position, then form upper and lower bowed lobes meeting the axis at a right reference position. These roughly paired lobes straddle the net crossing. The right lower lobe approaches the net trough. They carry no independent force label or given number.
observations.requiredRelationship: Retain the source solid/dashed distinction and shared-frame guide relationship; do not promote these construction strokes to an extra physical curve, numerical datum or named law.

observations.pixelFacts: Only F, r, 0 and r0 are mathematical labels. The three other labels are source Chinese force descriptions. The plot ends on the right with its force tails still on their respective sides of zero; no finite zero-force cutoff is marked.
observations.requiredRelationship: Use readable English force labels and mathematical symbols, remove source-language visual leakage, preserve qualitative behavior without invented physical numbers or a finite cutoff.

textCompatibilityFactsFromSourceOnly: The original prose explicitly states repulsion positive, attraction negative, net zero at r0, positive below r0, negative above r0, and F tending to zero as r tends to infinity.
The original prose describes the thick small curve segment as approximately straight for small displacement, not exact linearity over the entire curve.
modernAdditionsToJudgeSeparately: English labels, component-sign annotations, a legend or explicit short-range/long-range directions may clarify existing facts but are not source pixels.
A deterministic smooth qualitative construction may regularize the scan; it must preserve the source relationships without claiming measured values or a specific physical force law.
